formulation.rationale: This child contains the single canonical insulin glargine record whose concentration/product is unspecified. No further split is possible without changing the canonical medication identity; concentration-specific U-100 versus U-300 timing is therefore not selected.

comparisons.checked_locators: Perioperative Care, insulin therapy adjustments; Insulin Therapy Recommendations 16.8 and 16.9
comparisons.note: ADA provides class-level long-acting basal-insulin guidance that remains applicable even when the glargine concentration is not identified.

comparisons.checked_locators: Table 2, Basal insulin (long-acting insulin analog: Glargine); Summary of evidence before Important note 11
comparisons.note: The joint statement distinguishes standard glargine from glargine U-300 and gives different preprocedure timing. Because the canonical medication does not identify concentration, the source does not yield one unambiguous concentration-specific instruction for this record.

comparisons.checked_locators: Recommendations Before Colonoscopy > Patient Education and Navigation
comparisons.note: USMSTF does not provide a product-specific insulin-glargine dose and directs individualized antihyperglycemic medication planning with the prescribing clinician.

recommendations.qualifier: long-acting basal insulin analogue; concentration unspecified
recommendations.timing_text: On the evening before surgery, reduce long-acting basal insulin analogs to 75–80% of the usual dose
recommendations.strength: not separately graded in this narrative instruction
recommendations.certainty: not separately graded in this narrative instruction
recommendations.applicability: Long-acting basal insulin analogue before surgery when the exact glargine concentration has not been identified.
recommendations.exceptions: Current SBD/SBA/ABESO guidance gives a longer adjustment window for glargine U-300, so identifying the actual product/concentration remains clinically important.
recommendations.summary: ADA recommends reducing long-acting basal insulin analogues to 75–80% of the usual dose on the evening before surgery.

recommendations.timing_text: Basal insulin or a basal plus bolus correction insulin plan is the preferred treatment
recommendations.applicability: Noncritically ill patient with poor oral intake or taking nothing by mouth.
recommendations.exceptions: The passage does not identify a concentration-specific glargine dose.
recommendations.summary: ADA retains basal insulin as part of the preferred insulin plan during poor oral intake or NPO status.

recommendations.qualifier: postprocedure poor oral intake or NPO
recommendations.timing_text: Basal insulin or a basal plus bolus correction insulin plan is the preferred treatment
recommendations.applicability: Postprocedure patient with poor oral intake or still NPO.
recommendations.exceptions: No fixed glargine restart time or concentration-specific dose is stated.
recommendations.summary: When oral intake remains poor or the patient remains NPO, ADA retains basal insulin in the preferred insulin plan.

recommendations.timing_text: an insulin plan with basal, prandial, and correction components is the preferred treatment
recommendations.applicability: Postprocedure patient with adequate nutritional intake.
recommendations.exceptions: No fixed glargine restart time or concentration-specific dose is stated.
recommendations.summary: With adequate nutritional intake, ADA includes basal insulin as part of the preferred insulin plan.

scenario_coverage.reason: ADA provides a class-level long-acting basal-insulin adjustment that does not require knowing glargine concentration.
ADA retains basal insulin during NPO or poor oral intake.
ADA includes basal insulin in preferred regimens for poor/NPO and adequate nutritional intake states.

open_questions.text: The actual insulin glargine product and concentration must be identified before applying concentration-specific guidance because SBD/SBA/ABESO recommends a longer 48–72-hour adjustment window for U-300 than for standard glargine.
USMSTF does not provide a colonoscopy-specific glargine dose and directs individualized antihyperglycemic management with the prescribing clinician.

editorial.notes: Unreviewed evidence package for a concentration-unspecified canonical glargine record. Only concentration-agnostic society guidance is converted into recommendations; concentration-specific SBD guidance is intentionally not selected.
